verses.text: David the king said to all the assembly, “Solomon my son, whom alone God has chosen, is yet young and tender, and the work is great; for the palace is not for man, but for Yahweh God.

Now I have prepared with all my might for the house of my God the gold for the things of gold, the silver for the things of silver, the brass for the things of brass, iron for the things of iron, and wood for the things of wood; also onyx stones, stones to be set, stones for inlaid work, of various colors, all kinds of precious stones, and marble stones in abundance.

In addition, because I have set my affection on the house of my God, since I have a treasure of my own of gold and silver, I give it to the house of my God, over and above all that I have prepared for the holy house,
even three thousand talents of gold,  of the gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents  of refined silver, with which to overlay the walls of the houses;

of gold for the things of gold, and of silver for the things of silver, and for all kinds of work to be made by the hands of artisans. Who then offers willingly to consecrate himself today to Yahweh?”
Then the princes of the fathers’ households, and the princes of the tribes of Israel, and the captains of thousands and of hundreds, with the rulers over the king’s work, offered willingly;

and they gave for the service of God’s house of gold five thousand talents  and ten thousand darics,  of silver ten thousand talents, of brass eighteen thousand talents, and of iron one hundred thousand talents.
People with whom precious stones were found gave them to the treasure of Yahweh’s house, under the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite.
Then the people rejoiced, because they offered willingly, because with a perfect heart they offered willingly to Yahweh; and David the king also rejoiced with great joy.
Therefore David blessed Yahweh before all the assembly; and David said, “You are blessed, Yahweh, the God of Israel our father, forever and ever.

Yours, Yahweh, is the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory, and the majesty! For all that is in the heavens and in the earth is yours. Yours is the kingdom, Yahweh, and you are exalted as head above all.
Both riches and honor come from you, and you rule over all! In your hand is power and might! It is in your hand to make great, and to give strength to all!
Now therefore, our God, we thank you, and praise your glorious name.
But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly as this? For all things come from you, and of your own have we given you.
For we are strangers before you, and foreigners, as all our fathers were. Our days on the earth are as a shadow, and there is no remaining.
Yahweh our God, all this store that we have prepared to build you a house for your holy name comes from your hand, and is all your own.

I know also, my God, that you try the heart, and have pleasure in uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have willingly offered all these things. Now I have seen with joy your people, who are present here, offer willingly to you.
Yahweh, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Israel, our fathers, keep this desire forever in the thoughts of the heart of your people, and prepare their heart for you;
and give to Solomon my son a perfect heart, to keep your commandments, your testimonies, and your statutes, and to do all these things, and to build the palace, for which I have made provision.”

Then David said to all the assembly, “Now bless Yahweh your God!” All the assembly blessed Yahweh, the God of their fathers, and bowed down their heads and prostrated themselves before Yahweh and the king.

They sacrificed sacrifices to Yahweh, and offered burnt offerings to Yahweh, on the next day after that day, even one thousand bulls, one thousand rams, and one thousand lambs, with their drink offerings and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel,
and ate and drank before Yahweh on that day with great gladness. They made Solomon the son of David king the second time, and anointed him before Yahweh to be prince, and Zadok to be priest.
Then Solomon sat on the throne of Yahweh as king instead of David his father, and prospered; and all Israel obeyed him.
All the princes, the mighty men, and also all of the sons of king David submitted themselves to Solomon the king.
Yahweh magnified Solomon exceedingly in the sight of all Israel, and gave to him such royal majesty as had not been on any king before him in Israel.
Now David the son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.
The time that he reigned over Israel was forty years; he reigned seven years in Hebron, and he reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
He died at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor; and Solomon his son reigned in his place.
Now the acts of David the king, first and last, behold, they are written in the history of Samuel the seer, and in the history of Nathan the prophet, and in the history of Gad the seer,
with all his reign and his might, and the times that went over him, and over Israel, and over all the kingdoms of the countries.

footnotes.content: David stands before Israel and names the truth plainly: Solomon is young, the work is vast, and the house is not for human glory but for the Lord. This is a father's honest word to his people—not flattery of the heir, but sober naming of what matters.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David catalogs the materials gathered—gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, onyx, gems, marble—with the care of a man who has given his whole mind to one great work. Notice the abundance of marble stones: the house will stand, and stand beautiful. This is stewardship made visible.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I have set my affection on the house of my God." The king speaks of love, not duty. He holds treasure in his hands and gives it freely because his heart has chosen to belong to the Lord's house. Affection makes the gift weightless.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three thousand talents of gold from Ophir, seven thousand talents of refined silver—these are real figures, real weight, the fruit of a kingdom's labor offered to the Lord. The walls themselves will shimmer with the king's faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David ends with a question, not a command: "Who then offers willingly to consecrate himself today to Yahweh?" He has shown his own hand open; now he invites his people into the same choice. Generous leadership asks, not demands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The princes, tribe leaders, captains, and rulers all stepped forward—not as subjects commanded, but as men who saw their king's heart and answered with their own. The best gift is always the one others freely choose to echo.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Five thousand talents of gold, ten thousand darics, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand of brass, one hundred thousand of iron—the congregation's offering dwarfs even the king's. When people see the heart of their leader, they open their own hands wide.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "People with whom precious stones were found gave them to the treasure." A line easy to pass over, yet it shows how far the giving rippled—common folk, holders of rare things, placed their treasures in Jehiel's trust and the Lord's house.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The people rejoiced because they gave willingly, and with a perfect heart. David also rejoiced—not in the amount gathered, but in seeing his nation's hearts turn toward the Lord with joy. That's a king's true victory.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David turns now to bless the Lord before all the assembly, naming Him the God of Israel from father to father. In the midst of triumph, the old king bows and points the people's gaze upward, not to his own name or Solomon's, but to Yahweh forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Yours is the greatness, the power, the glory..." David speaks the truth he has lived: the kingdom rises and falls in God's hand. Everything in heaven and earth already belongs to Him. We hold nothing; we steward what He lends.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Riches and honor come from Him; all power rests in His hand. David speaks as one who has held both and felt them slip away. In age, he knows that making great and giving strength belong only to the Lord—and that's the only security a king truly has.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In a single breath, thanks and praise—David holds both the wonder and the weight of God's name. His life has been a long conversation with that glorious name, and here at the last, gratitude is all he knows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly as this?" The king does not marvel at his own strength or his nation's wealth, but at the truth that every gift already belonged to the Lord. Humility is the only honest response.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "We are strangers and foreigners...our days are as a shadow." David faces the brevity of life without bitterness, holding his fleeting years gently. All the gold and silver, all the marble will outlast him—a comfort to a man nearing the end.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All that David has prepared and given comes from God's own hand first. The store, the treasure, the work—all of it begins with Him and returns to Him. The king is merely the channel through which the Lord's abundance flows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David confesses that God tries the heart and loves uprightness—and that in uprightness of his own heart, he has offered all these things willingly. He stakes his life on this: that the Lord knows the intention, not just the gift.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David prays that the Lord will keep this desire forever in his people's hearts—not the desire for gold or greatness, but the desire to turn toward God and let Him prepare their hearts. That is a father's deepest prayer for his nation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: For Solomon, David asks not for wealth or power, but for a perfect heart to keep God's commandments and build the house with faithfulness. A father's truest blessing is not strength, but the will to obey the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David calls the assembly to bless the Lord their God. They bow, kneel, and prostrate themselves before the Lord and the king—a people united in reverence. The physical posture speaks the inward truth: we belong to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One thousand bulls, one thousand rams, one thousand lambs—an astounding sacrifice offered the next day with abundance of drink offerings for all Israel. The celebration is not private; it embraces the whole nation in one great act of worship.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Solomon is anointed king before the Lord a second time, with Zadok confirmed as priest. The ritual ordination seals what the people have already chosen—and what David has already prepared in his heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Solomon sits on the throne of the Lord, not merely the throne of Israel. He prospers, and all Israel obeys—not through force, but because the transition is wrapped in faithfulness and joy. A kingdom at peace with its succession.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Princes, mighty men, even David's own sons bowed to Solomon. The hardest test of a king's legacy is not his own power, but whether his children and captains willingly honor his heir. Here, the transition is seamless.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord magnified Solomon in the sight of all Israel and gave him royal majesty such as no king before him had received. The young man steps into a throne already prepared by his father's prayer and the Lord's favor.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "David the son of Jesse reigned over all Israel." A single line to anchor the whole reign—the shepherd boy raised up, the king of Israel, named by his father's name and his lineage, now passing the crown to the next generation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Forty years of reign—seven in Hebron, thirty-three in Jerusalem. The numbers mark the arc of a life poured out in service. Each year is a stone laid in the foundation he leaves behind.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David died at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor. Not every soul leaves like this—satisfied, blessed, and ready. Solomon reigns in his place, and the kingdom does not skip a beat. The old king can rest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The acts of David are recorded—in the history of Samuel, Nathan, and Gad, the seers who walked with him. His life is written not by courtiers, but by prophets who knew the Lord's hand upon him. That is the truest chronicle.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in these final words: a life's reign and might, the times that went over him and over his people, recorded for remembrance. We too live in times the Lord ordains; we too are written in His memory, though our names fade from earthly pages.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
